strategy_title: Autotune large XBLOCK causes register spill and 3.7x slowdown
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with large XBLOCK values (512–2048) to a kernel that previously used XBLOCK=128 caused registers per thread to jump from 22 to 48, collapsing theoretical occupancy from 100% to 62.5% (Block Limit Registers dropped from 21 to 5 blocks/SM) and increasing waves per SM from 3.3 to 10.6. The autotune grid was left fixed at the original small-block grid size (cdiv(xnumel, 128)) rather than being updated to a lambda using meta['XBLOCK'], so the kernel ran the same number of blocks but with far more work per block and severe register pressure, resulting in 6.8x more executed instructions and 3.7x longer duration. When increasing XBLOCK via autotune, the launch grid must be a lambda over meta['XBLOCK']; a static grid computed with the old small block size defeats the purpose and causes massive over-subscription.
applicable_when: Never apply this specific pattern (static grid + autotune XBLOCK). The corrected pattern (lambda grid) is applicable when LaunchConfiguration rule fires with >15% partial-wave waste and registers per thread are low (<30), leaving headroom to increase block size without register pressure.
do_not_apply_when: Do not add @triton.autotune with large XBLOCK configs when the kernel already uses 22+ registers per thread, as doubling XBLOCK tends to push register count above 32–48, cutting theoretical occupancy by 37–62% and negating any partial-wave savings. Also do not use a static grid when adding autotune — always use a lambda grid.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: when using @triton.autotune, the launch grid MUST be a Python lambda that reads meta['XBLOCK'] (or whichever constexpr is being tuned). A static grid computed before the autotune runs will not adapt to the selected config, causing the kernel to launch with the wrong number of blocks.

strategy_title: Autotuning XBLOCK upward regresses when register pressure increases
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with larger XBLOCK configs (512–2048) caused the autotuner to select a configuration that increased registers per thread from 22 to 32, reducing the block limit from 21 to 16 blocks/SM. Although achieved occupancy rose from 64.6% to 80.7% and compute throughput improved from 43% to 63%, the total executed instruction count nearly doubled (2.37M → 4.50M) and kernel duration increased from 6.98 µs to 9.02 µs — a 29% regression. The grid was kept fixed at cdiv(xnumel, 128) in the launch call rather than being made dynamic via a lambda, so the autotuner selected a larger XBLOCK but the grid was not recalculated, causing each block to process more elements and issue far more instructions. The structural anti-pattern is passing a static grid computed with the old XBLOCK while letting autotune vary XBLOCK freely, and not accounting for the register spill caused by larger tile sizes.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: fixed grid, fixed XBLOCK=128, 22 regs/thread
grid = (cdiv(xnumel, 128),)  # static, not updated with autotuned XBLOCK
kernel[grid](args, xnumel=893760, XBLOCK=128)
fast_pseudocode:
# CORRECT pattern if autotuning XBLOCK (not applied here — this is the fix that was missing):
grid = lambda meta: (cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)  # dynamic grid
kernel[grid](args, xnumel=893760)  # XBLOCK comes from autotune config
applicable_when: Kernel has a partial wave (LaunchConfiguration NCU rule triggered), low achieved occupancy vs theoretical, and low register usage (<24 regs/thread) leaving headroom for larger tiles without spill.
do_not_apply_when: The launch grid is not updated dynamically to match the autotuned XBLOCK — this causes the autotuner to pick large XBLOCK while the grid remains sized for the original small XBLOCK, multiplying instruction count. Also avoid when register usage is near the block limit boundary (e.g., 22 regs/thread near the 21-block/SM limit), as larger tiles may push registers to 32+, reducing block limit and negating occupancy gains.
framework_notes: In Triton, when using @triton.autotune with XBLOCK as a tunable parameter, the grid MUST be a lambda: `grid = lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)`. Using a static grid computed with the old XBLOCK is a correctness/performance bug — the kernel will be launched with too many blocks, each processing a larger tile, causing instruction count explosion.
